definitions.explanation: A situation that is hard to deal with (na-adjective use).

examples.japanese: {大変|たいへん}おいしいです。
{大変|たいへん}お{世話|せわ}になりました。
examples.english: Thank you very much for everything.

examples.japanese: {大変|たいへん}{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません。
{大変|たいへん}よくできました。
{先生|せんせい}に{大変|たいへん}お{世話|せわ}になりました。{卒業|そつぎょう}できたのは{先生|せんせい}のおかげです。
examples.english: The teacher helped me a great deal. I was able to graduate thanks to the teacher.

examples.japanese: {大変|たいへん}な{仕事|しごと}ですね。
{子供|こども}が{三人|さんにん}いて、{大変|たいへん}です。
examples.english: I have three children, so it's hard.

examples.japanese: {大変|たいへん}な{時|とき}に{助|たす}けてくれてありがとう。
examples.english: Thank you for helping me during a difficult time.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{残業|ざんぎょう}があって{大変|たいへん}です。{休|やす}む{時間|じかん}がありません。{疲|つか}れました。
examples.english: I have overtime every day, so it's tough. I don't have time to rest. I'm exhausted.

notes:
{大変|たいへん} has two main uses: "very" (adverb) and "difficult/tough" (na-adjective).

ADVERB USE (very):
- {大変|たいへん}おいしい: very delicious
- {大変|たいへん}お{世話|せわ}になりました: thank you very much for your help
- {大変|たいへん}{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません: I'm terribly sorry

NA-ADJECTIVE USE (difficult):
- {大変|たいへん}な{仕事|しごと}: difficult work
- {大変|たいへん}ですね: that's tough (expression of sympathy)
- {大変|たいへん}な{思|おも}いをする: to have a hard time

REGISTER:
As an adverb meaning "very," {大変|たいへん} is more formal/polite than とても. Common in formal speech and writing.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- とても: very (neutral)
- {非常|ひじょう}に: extremely (formal)
- すごく: very (casual)
